name: The Madej Oak

location.address: Roadside on the road to Bielinek/Piasek (route 125/126), upper part of Lubiechów Dolny, gmina Cedynia, Gryfino County, West Pomeranian Voivodeship, Poland

access: Free. Stands right beside a public road in the village, no permission needed; the retaining wall it grows from is visible from the roadside.
transport: No public transport nearby; rural village reached by car, roughly 60km from Szczecin (well outside the day-trip boundary of any city we currently publish).
story:
Somebody built a brick wall to stop this oak sliding downhill. When the road through the upper end of Lubiechow Dolny was widened, before the Second World War, the slope beneath the tree was cut away, and the roadmen laid up a retaining wall of clinker brick to hold the ground the trunk was standing on. It worked, and the oak is now slowly taking the wall back: the base of the trunk has begun to grow over the brickwork and close around it.

The trunk measured 599 centimetres round in 2021, under a crown twenty-two metres up. Nobody has dated it, and girth is the only basis there is, which makes the honest band a wide one. A listed pedunculate oak of 580 centimetres elsewhere in the region is officially described as over 250 years old; the measured recent growth of the oak a hundred metres down the same road, about a centimetre and a half a year, would put a trunk this size nearer 400. Somewhere in there.

The road was a German road when the wall went up. In 1945 the border moved to the Oder a few kilometres west of here and everyone in the village was replaced. Cedynia's council protected this oak and its neighbour in November 2013 and gave neither of them a name. Madej and Pietrek are what the people living here call them.
how_to_recognise: You can recognise it by the clinker-brick retaining wall at its foot, which the base of the trunk is growing over. It stands at the top end of the village, a hundred metres above the Pietrek Oak, and is 5.99 metres round.

name: The Pietrek Oak

location.address: Roadside on the road to Bielinek/Piasek (route 125/126), about 100m below the Madej Oak, Lubiechów Dolny, gmina Cedynia, Gryfino County, West Pomeranian Voivodeship, Poland

access: Free. Grows about half a metre from a public road, right of way, no permission needed.
transport: No public transport nearby; rural village reached by car, roughly 60km from Szczecin (well outside the day-trip boundary of any city we currently publish).
story:
A lorry hit this oak, and the damage is still the first thing you see. It grows about half a metre from the edge of a public road on a ravine slope that tilts toward the tarmac, which is a poor address for a trunk 618 centimetres round, and the collision left a large dead patch on the north-west face. There is old tree surgery on it. The oak is still putting on wood regardless: the same trunk was 608 centimetres in 2013 and 618 when it was measured in October 2021, a centimetre and a half a year.

Twenty metres tall, ten metres of crown, and the thicker of the two protected oaks in this village by nineteen centimetres. Cedynia's council gave both of them monument status in November 2013 without naming either. Pietrek is the village's own name for this one. Nobody has dated it, and girth is the only basis anyone has, which puts it somewhere between 250 and 450 years old and no narrower than that.

Three nature reserves lie within five hundred metres. One of them, Bielinek above the Oder, holds the only stand of downy oak in Poland, a dry southern species with no business this far north, growing a short walk from two ordinary Polish oaks that have outlasted a border change.
how_to_recognise: You can recognise it by the large dead patch on the north-west side of the trunk where a lorry struck it, and by the trunk itself, 6.18 metres round. It stands half a metre from the road, a hundred metres below the Madej Oak.

name: The Jeremi Oak

location.address: On Zbocze Fordońskie (the Fordoń escarpment) near the Tatrzańskie housing estate, Fordon district, Bydgoszcz, Kuyavian-Pomeranian Voivodeship, Poland

access: Free. Stands in open ground on the Fordoń escarpment, on the public walking trail named after Jeremi Przybora (Szlak im. Jeremiego Przybory, which connects Fordon to the Myslecinek forest park); no permission needed.
transport: In the Fordon district of Bydgoszcz, on the hillside above the Vistula near the Tatrzańskie estate; reachable by city bus to Fordon then a short uphill walk.
story:
Bydgoszcz voted an oak into first place before it named anything else that year. The city's own 'Tree of the Year' poll gave 932 votes, a local record, to a pedunculate oak on the escarpment above the Vistula in Fordon.

The tree already had three names before that vote. The council itself calls it Jeremi, in a 2011 protection order honouring Jeremi Przybora, the poet and co-founder of the satirical Kabaret Starszych Panow, who grew up on a nearby estate and never lost his attachment to the hillside. Locals call it something darker, Wisielec, the Hanged Man, and something grander, Dab Napoleona, Napoleon's Oak, on the strength of a story that the emperor watched his own troops cross the river from beneath its crown during the 1812 campaign into Russia. Nobody has dated the tree to say whether it could have stood that long ago; that is tradition, not a fact this page can confirm. Archaeologists do think the hillside was once a medieval motte-and-bailey fortress.

The trunk is a modest 305 centimetres round, well short of the 600 centimetre oaks the region protects elsewhere, which puts only a broad band on it, a century and a half to two and a half centuries, and no narrower. The crown reads windswept rather than tidy, shaped by the open ground it stands on.

It stands on a public trail named for Przybora himself, connecting Fordon to the Myslecinek forest, free to reach by city bus and a short climb.
how_to_recognise: You can recognise it by the windswept, ragged crown atop a 305cm trunk, standing alone in open ground on the Fordon escarpment above the Vistula, on the walking trail named for Jeremi Przybora near the Tatrzanskie estate.
